objective: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on her leg.

patient_info.History: The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg
Secondary_Symptoms: Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders
History of ant bite at the site of the lesion
Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities
Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs

Past_Medical_History: Treated for anterior uveitis 8 months ago
patient_info.Social_History: Recently returned from a visit to Wisconsin 2 months ago.
patient_info.Review_of_Systems: No additional systemic symptoms mentioned.

Skin_Examination.Inspection: A 4-cm tender ulcerative lesion on the anterior right leg with a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders. Pitting pedal edema is noted along with dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.
Skin_Examination.Palpation: Tenderness over the lesion. Femoral and pedal pulses palpable bilaterally.

Histopathology.Findings: Neutrophilic infiltration without infection, consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum.

objective: Evaluate and manage a patient presenting with chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination.

patient_info.History: The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Bladder discomfort relieved by voiding

patient_info.Past_Medical_History: Significant for bipolar disorder, currently managed with lithium.
patient_info.Social_History: Married and sexually active with her husband. No significant alcohol, tobacco, or recreational drug use.
patient_info.Review_of_Systems: Denies fever, hematuria, back pain, pelvic pain other than with intercourse, and any recent infections.

Abdominal_Examination.Palpation: Tenderness to palpation of the suprapubic region, no masses palpated

Pelvic_Examination.Findings: No external lesions, vaginal discharge, or obvious masses. Cervix appears normal upon speculum examination. Bimanual examination reveals normal uterus and adnexa, with discomfort noted on palpation of the bladder region.

objective: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with a pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities.

patient_info.History: The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities

patient_info.Past_Medical_History: No history of serious illness. No known drug allergies. Takes no medications.
patient_info.Social_History: College student studying graphic design. Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. No recreational drug use.
patient_info.Review_of_Systems: Denies recent fever, joint pains, weight loss, or changes in bowel habits.

Skin_Examination.Inspection: Bilateral erythematous, scaly, and crusted lesions localized to the upper extremities.
Skin_Examination.Palpation: No warmth or induration. The lesions are slightly raised and rough to touch.

Skin_Biopsy.Findings: Intraepidermal accumulation of edematous fluid and widening of intercellular spaces between keratinocytes.

objective: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with a concerning rash and recent health changes.

patient_info.History: The patient presents with a rash that started last night, finding it very concerning. He does not recall being exposed to any new environmental stimuli such as detergents or plants like poison ivy. He mentions he recently started seeing a primary care provider for arthritis management and a new onset cough.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Rash on the upper half of the back
Secondary_Symptoms: Unaware of exposure to new environmental stimuli

patient_info.Past_Medical_History: Has been diagnosed with arthritis. No other significant past medical history has been mentioned.
patient_info.Social_History: The patient didn't provide any specific social history details during the initial consultation.
patient_info.Review_of_Systems: Reports a new onset cough along with skin and mucosal changes but denies fever, shortness of breath, joint pains, gastrointestinal symptoms, or recent illnesses.

Skin_Examination.General: Coalescing erythematous macules, bullae, desquamation noted.
Skin_Examination.Distribution: Localized to the upper half of the back.
Skin_Examination.Mucous_Membranes: Ulcers and erythema present in oropharynx.

Cardiopulmonary_Exam.Cardiac: Normal rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops.
Cardiopulmonary_Exam.Pulmonary: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, no wheezes, rales, or rhonchi.

physical_exam.Abdominal_Exam: Soft, non-tender, no hepatosplenomegaly, normoactive bowel sounds throughout.

Skin_Biopsy.Findings: Epidermal necrosis and detachment, consistent with severe drug reaction.

objective: Assess and manage a young adult male presenting with aggressive behavior, altered mental status, and autonomic dysregulation.

patient_info.History: The patient's roommates report that he has been displaying increasingly aggressive and unusual behavior. They mention that he has been under significant stress due to final exams and has become more reclusive. Earlier this evening, he exhibited extreme irritability, yelled at his computer, broke it, and then spent several hours at the gym.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Aggressive behavior and irritability
Secondary_Symptoms: Prolonged physical activity (several hours at the gym)

patient_info.Past_Medical_History: No significant past medical history reported by the roommates.
patient_info.Social_History: Stress from upcoming final exams. No other social history provided.
patient_info.Review_of_Systems: Roommates did not report any fever, vomiting, diarrhea, dysuria, or flank pain prior to the event. During the physical exam, the patient is noted to be diaphoretic.

objective: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with wrist pain and difficulty in hand movement.

patient_info.History: The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Pain in the right thumb and wrist, radiating to the elbow
Secondary_Symptoms: Pain improves with ice pack application

patient_info.Past_Medical_History: Previous fall on right outstretched hand six months ago. No significant other medical history.
patient_info.Social_History: Patient is a mother of an infant, leading a relatively active lifestyle. Does not smoke or consume alcohol regularly.
patient_info.Review_of_Systems: Denies any fever, weight loss, or other joint problems.

Right_Hand_Examination.Inspection: Swelling over the radial styloid with no redness
Right_Hand_Examination.Palpation: Tenderness over the radial styloid. No crepitus.

Special_Tests.Finkelstein's_Test: Positive, eliciting pain on the radial side of the wrist when grasping the thumb and exerting longitudinal traction towards the ulnar side.

Right_Hand_Examination.Range_of_Motion: Normal range of motion of finger joints. No swelling, redness, or tenderness in other joints.

objective: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with concerns from her mother regarding attention issues and a change in behavior.

patient_info.History: The patient's mother reports her daughter has been performing poorly academically since starting high school. The mother is concerned about her daughter's lack of communication and perceives her daughter as having attention issues.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Mother reports lackluster grades and perceived attention issues.
Secondary_Symptoms: Social withdrawal from previously enjoyed activities
Expresses unhappiness with current social situation
Denies suicidal ideation or intention to harm others

patient_info.Past_Medical_History: No significant past medical or psychiatric history.

Social_History.Substance_Use: Denies smoking cigarettes or marijuana use.
Social_History.Interests: Mentions disinterest in previously enjoyed social activities like hanging out with peers from the cheerleading squad.

patient_info.Review_of_Systems: Negative for signs of depression or anxiety such as sleep disturbances, significant weight change, or excessive worries.

Mental_Status_Examination.Appearance: Casually dressed, chewing gum, appears her stated age.
Mental_Status_Examination.Behavior: Cooperative, but shows irritability in context of discussion about her mother.
Mental_Status_Examination.Thought_Content: Denies hallucinations, delusions, or suicidal ideation.
Mental_Status_Examination.Cognition: Alert and oriented to time, place, and person.

Screening_Tests.Depression_Screening: Patient scores on the lower end, indicating no significant signs of depression.
Screening_Tests.Anxiety_Screening: Patient scores do not suggest an anxiety disorder.
Screening_Tests.ADHD_Screening: Patient's symptoms do not align with a diagnosis of ADHD.

objective: Evaluate the patient with persistent vomiting and chest pain, perform necessary examinations, and establish a diagnosis.

patient_info.History: The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Persistent, forceful vomiting

patient_info.Past_Medical_History: Significant for Lyme disease, currently being treated with doxycycline.
patient_info.Social_History: Reported alcohol use; found next to an empty bottle of vodka.
patient_info.Review_of_Systems: Patient appears toxic and in acute distress, unable to provide a comprehensive review of systems.

Chest_Examination.Inspection: Fullness at the base of the neck
Chest_Examination.Auscultation: Crunching, rasping sound heard over the chest
Chest_Examination.Palpation: Possible crepitus on palpation of the chest and neck

Chest_X-ray.Findings: Free mediastinal air visible, suggesting perforation

objective: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with a chronic wound on his right lower leg.

patient_info.History: The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Large wound on the right lower leg
Secondary_Symptoms: Family history of similar leg problems

patient_info.Past_Medical_History: Deep vein thrombosis in the right leg 5 years prior. No other significant medical history.
patient_info.Social_History: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works as an accountant.
patient_info.Review_of_Systems: Denies fever, recent injuries, heart disease, or diabetes.

Leg_Examination.Inspection: Large ulcer on the right lower leg, presence of varicose veins
Leg_Examination.Palpation: Edema in both legs, more pronounced in the right leg
Leg_Examination.Pulse: Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses are palpable but diminished in the right leg
Leg_Examination.Skin: Skin around the wound is discolored with evidence of chronic changes such as pigmentation

Doppler_Ultrasound_Lower_Limb.Findings: Evidence of venous reflux and obstruction in superficial and deep venous systems of the right leg

objective: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with blisters on her forearm and ulcers on mucosal surfaces.

patient_info.History: The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Multiple, flaccid blisters on the volar surface of the forearm
Secondary_Symptoms: Ulcers on the buccal, gingival, and vulvar mucosa
Pain in the left cheek when eating

patient_info.Drug_History: Recently started captopril, stopped taking meloxicam 2 weeks ago.
patient_info.Social_History: Has started hiking in the woods on weekends. No relevant travel history.
patient_info.Review_of_Systems: No recent illnesses, denies fever, respiratory symptoms, or gastrointestinal symptoms.

Skin_Examination.Inspection: Multiple, flaccid blisters on the volar surface of the forearm, with 10% total body surface area involvement.
Skin_Examination.Palpation: Skin separation (Nikolsky sign positive) when lightly stroked.
Skin_Examination.Mucosal_Examination: Ulcers present on the buccal, gingival, and vulvar mucosa.

Direct_Immunofluorescence.Findings: Intercellular IgG and C3 deposition within the epidermis.

objective: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with progressively worsening shortness of breath over the past 2 months.

patient_info.History: The patient reports progressively worsening shortness of breath for the past 2 months, which does not occur at rest. He occasionally experiences a dry cough but denies having fever, chills, or night sweats.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Progressively worsening shortness of breath

patient_info.Past_Medical_History: The patient is previously healthy with no significant past medical history.
patient_info.Social_History: Smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for the past 40 years. Drinks a beer daily with occasional increase on weekends. No illicit drug use.
patient_info.Review_of_Systems: Denies any other systemic complaints.

Lung_Examination.Inspection: Normal chest wall movement, no use of accessory muscles at rest.
Lung_Examination.Auscultation: Prolonged expiratory phase and end-expiratory wheezing.

objective: Assess and diagnose the pediatric patient presenting with generalized rash, fever, and malaise.

patient_info.History: The patient presents with a generalized rash for 3 days, accompanied by severe itching. He has experienced difficulty sleeping due to discomfort. Additionally, symptoms include fever, headache, and muscle pain. The onset of a runny nose was noted 5 days ago, which receded with over-the-counter medications. The patient recently returned from a camping trip 1 week ago and attends a daycare center regularly.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Generalized rash over face, trunk, and extremities

patient_info.Review_of_Systems: Denies any respiratory distress, no reported vomiting or diarrhea.

Skin_Examination.Inspection: Observation of several macules, papules, and crusted lesions across the face, trunk, and extremities. A few fluid-filled vesicles noted over the abdomen and back.

objective: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with intermittent flank pain and a history of multiple urinary tract infections.

patient_info.History: The patient reports a 5-month history of intermittent flank pain. She mentions having had five urinary tract infections over the past 2 years. She has not experienced any recent fever, weight loss, or significant changes in urinary or bowel habits.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Intermittent flank pain
Secondary_Symptoms: No noticeable changes in urinary or bowel habits

patient_info.Past_Medical_History: No significant past medical history apart from recurrent urinary tract infections.
patient_info.Social_History: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works as a middle school teacher.
patient_info.Review_of_Systems: Denies any recent fever, trauma to the back or abdomen, cough, shortness of breath, rash, or joint pain.

Abdominal_Examination.Percussion: No ascites. Bilateral flank dullness could be elicited.
Abdominal_Examination.Palpation: Bilateral, nontender upper abdominal masses palpable. No palpable liver or spleen.

Renal_Ultrasonography.Findings: Bilaterally enlarged kidneys with multiple parenchymal anechoic masses.

objective: Evaluate and diagnose the pediatric patient presenting with fever and a pruritic rash.

patient_info.History: The patient has been brought in by his mother due to a 2-day history of fever and a rash. The rash initially appeared on his trunk and subsequently spread to his face and extremities. The child has not received any childhood vaccinations as his parents are opposed to them.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Fever and pruritic rash
Secondary_Symptoms: Rash starting on the trunk and spreading to face and extremities
Mother reports the child seems more irritable than usual

patient_info.Past_Medical_History: No significant past medical history. Unvaccinated.
patient_info.Social_History: Lives at home with both parents and one older sibling. No recent travel history.
patient_info.Review_of_Systems: Denies any cough, runny nose, vomiting, or diarrhea. The patient has been eating and drinking less than usual according to the mother.

Dermatologic_Examination.Inspection: Diffuse maculopapular rash noted on the trunk, spreading to the face and extremities. Some vesicles observed.
Dermatologic_Examination.Palpation: The rash is pruritic but no significant warmth or tenderness on palpation.

objective: Assess, manage initially, and diagnose the patient post-motor vehicle collision with respiratory distress and subsequent pneumothorax.

patient_info.History: The patient was involved in a head-on collision as the front seat, unrestrained driver. He was brought to the emergency department with a low Glasgow Coma Scale and was intubated for airway protection. He initially received needle decompression and chest tube placement for a pneumothorax.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Recurrent pneumothorax on chest X-ray with a chest tube already in place.
Secondary_Symptoms: Subcutaneous emphysema in the clavicular area noted earlier
Stabilized after resuscitation but now shows signs of respiratory distress again

patient_info.Social_History: Unknown at this time due to the patient's condition.
patient_info.Review_of_Systems: Limited due to patient's unconscious state and intubation.

Neck_and_Chest_Examination.Inspection: Subcutaneous emphysema palpable around the neck and upper chest
Neck_and_Chest_Examination.Auscultation: Decreased breath sounds on the side of the injury
Neck_and_Chest_Examination.Palpation: Crepitus noted in the subcutaneous tissue of the neck and clavicular area

Chest_Radiography.Initial_Findings: Proper chest tube placement with resolution of the initial pneumothorax.
Chest_Radiography.Repeat_Findings: Recurrent pneumothorax with the chest tube still in place.

objective: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with a painless, nonpruritic skin lesion on her right thigh.

patient_info.History: The patient presents with a 1-month history of a painless, nonpruritic skin lesion on her right thigh. She initially thought it was an insect bite but noticed that it has slowly increased in size over the past weeks.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Painless, nonpruritic skin lesion on right thigh
Secondary_Symptoms: Slow increase in size over the past month

patient_info.Past_Medical_History: No significant past medical or dermatologic history.
patient_info.Social_History: Non-smoker, drinks socially. Works as a teacher.
patient_info.Review_of_Systems: Denies fever, weight loss, night sweats, or recent travel.

Skin_Examination.Inspection: A 0.8-cm hyperpigmented papule on the right thigh.
Skin_Examination.Palpation: The lesion retracts inward when squeezed (dimple sign).
Skin_Examination.Additional_Features: No discharge, erythema, or warmth surrounding the lesion.

Dermoscopic_Examination.Findings: Central white patch and peripheral pigment network, indicative of a benign process.

Biopsy.Histopathology: Positive for dermatofibroma, showing a benign proliferation of fibroblasts.

objective: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with sudden loss of consciousness and no prior history of neurological or cardiovascular problems.

patient_info.History: The patient experienced sudden loss of consciousness while pitching in a baseball game. No history of trauma associated with the event. The patient regained consciousness after receiving cardiopulmonary resuscitation.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Sudden loss of consciousness

patient_info.Social_History: Active, with regular participation in sports. No use of tobacco, alcohol, or recreational drugs reported.
patient_info.Review_of_Systems: Negative for headaches, seizures, chest pain, palpitations, shortness of breath, or dizziness prior to the event.

Echocardiogram.Findings: Left ventricular hypertrophy with septal thickening; reduced ventricular cavity size

Cardiac_MRI.Findings: Confirmatory findings of marked left ventricular hypertrophy, especially of the interventricular septum

Genetic_Testing.Findings: Positive for mutations associated with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy

objective: Assess and manage a 40-year-old woman who has presented with weakness and weight loss, and interpret her laboratory findings to make a diagnosis.

patient_info.History: The patient reports feeling weaker over the last few months and has noticed a decrease in her weight despite no changes in diet or exercise. She denies any changes in urinary frequency or pain during urination. She reports no history of diabetes or hypertension but is concerned about her kidney function due to a family history of kidney disease.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Generalized weakness

patient_info.Past_Medical_History: Denies diabetes, hypertension. No significant surgery history. Family history of kidney disease.
patient_info.Social_History: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially, works as a school teacher.
patient_info.Review_of_Systems: Denies fever, rash, changes in bowel habits, dysuria, or nocturia.

General_Examination.Skin: Normal turgor, no rashes or bruises

Cardiovascular_Examination.Heart_Sounds: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs

Respiratory_Examination.Lung_Sounds: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, no crackles or wheezes

Abdominal_Examination.Palpation: No tenderness or masses, kidneys not palpable

Neurological_Examination.Muscle_Strength: 5/5 in all extremities, though the patient reports feeling weak

objective: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with primary amenorrhea.

patient_info.History: The patient presents with a primary concern of having never had a menstrual period. She expresses anxiety about not experiencing menarche like her peers. Notable developmental milestones include breast development at age 13, alongside a growth spurt. The patient reports intermittent headaches with photosensitivity and nausea, effectively managed with ibuprofen. She has a history of competitive ice skating, denies any sexual activity, and family history includes migraine headaches in her mother and bipolar disorder in her sister.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Lack of menstruation

patient_info.Past_Medical_History: No significant past medical history. Reports development of secondary sexual characteristics at the expected age.
patient_info.Social_History: Competitive ice skater, no sexual activity, no medications or illicit substance use.
patient_info.Review_of_Systems: Positive for intermittent headaches; denies visual disturbances (beyond photosensitivity), no reported weight changes, or changes in appetite.

physical_exam.General_Examination: No acute distress. Developmental stage appropriate for age with breast and axillary hair Tanner stage IV.
physical_exam.Pelvic_Examination: Partially tolerant. External genitalia and the visible portion of the vaginal canal are unremarkable. Unable to perform a complete examination.

objective: Evaluate a 55-year-old man presenting with foot pain and cramping during exercise, and diagnose the underlying condition.

patient_info.History: The patient has been experiencing tingling pain in the sole of his right foot for the last 6 weeks, which occurs when he raises his foot above chest level during exercises. He started exercising regularly 2 months ago and notices his right calf cramps when using the incline feature on his treadmill, requiring him to stop frequently. The pain subsides after a few minutes of rest. He has been managing type 2 diabetes mellitus for 8 years. He is a smoker with a 34-year history of smoking two packs per day.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Tingling pain in the sole of the right foot during exercise
Secondary_Symptoms: Right calf cramps with incline exercise

patient_info.Past_Medical_History: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, managed with metformin for the past 8 years.
patient_info.Social_History: Smoking history of two packs per day for 34 years.
patient_info.Review_of_Systems: No other systemic symptoms reported.

Neurovascular_Examination.Straight_Leg_Raise_Test: Induces pallor and tingling pain in the right foot, without back pain
Neurovascular_Examination.Pulses: Femoral pulses palpable, right pedal pulses absent

Ankle-Brachial_Index.Right: Reduced, indicative of peripheral artery disease

Doppler_Ultrasound_Right_Lower_Extremity.Findings: Reduced blood flow and stenosis in the femoropopliteal artery segment
